chunks: From him, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he used to say:
The Qadeed (dried meat) is evil meat because it relaxes in the stomach and agitates every illness, and it does not benefit anything, but it harms it.

key_terms.الْقَدِيدُ: Dried meat, specifically salted and dried beef or camel meat.
key_terms.لَحْمُ سَوْءٍ: Evil or bad meat, indicating inferior quality or harmful nature.
key_terms.يَسْتَرْخِي: Relaxes or remains soft/unbroken down, referring to digestion.
key_terms.يُهَيِّجُ: Agitates or stimulates, causing irritation or activation of ailments.

ai.seo_question: What is the health ruling on dried meat (Qadeed) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) characterizes 'Al-Qadeed' (dried meat) as 'evil meat' due to its tendency to remain undigested and stimulate various ailments, reflecting the Shia emphasis on dietary hygiene as a foundation for spiritual and physical well-being. This narration underscores the practical medical wisdom found in the Ahl al-Bayt, linking specific food properties to broader health principles.
